raw_case_text:
A 31-year-old Caucasian female with ulcerative colitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, and cirrhosis presented with fever, chills, shortness of breath, dry cough, and chest pain for five days after being started on prednisone 40 mg daily and azathioprine 50 mg daily for autoimmune hepatitis two months earlier. She was born and raised in New York state and only travelled to Vermont and Florida. During the prior two weeks, she traveled to a hunting shack in northern New York and had been there twice before becoming ill. She had no personal or family history of tuberculosis and has had several prior negative PPDs during nursing school. On presentation, she was febrile to 102 F, pulse of 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, and blood pressure of 96/58 mmHg and required 2 liters oxygen to keep her saturation above 90%. Initial exam was benign with clear lungs. After blood and urine cultures were obtained, vancomycin and meropenem were started empirically. A paracentesis was not performed due to small ascitic fluid pockets. Initial chest X-ray showed trace left-sided pleural effusion without any evidence of infiltrates. Initial lab work showed ALT 62 U/L, AST 87 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 158 U/L, total bilirubin 13.2 mg/dL, INR of 2.9, WBC of 16,000/ul with 14,400/uL neutrophils, hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, and platelets of 167,000/uL. After a CT chest revealed small bilateral cavitary nodules the following day, vancomycin and meropenem were continued along with amphotericin being started with concern for a fungal infection (Figure 1).
Without clinical improvement, a CT guided biopsy of the necrotic pulmonary nodules was performed by interventional radiology three days after admission. The CT chest of the biopsy showed a new right upper lobe lesion (Figure 1) despite being on meropenem, vancomycin, and amphotericin. A bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage was performed the following day and Gram stain, fungal stain, and extensive cultures were all negative. With continued deterioration six days after the biopsy, a repeat CT chest showed increasing size and number of pulmonary nodules with ground glass opacities despite treatment with meropenem, vancomycin, and amphotericin. On day eleven of admission, cultures from the CT guided biopsy turned positive for Legionella. The antimicrobials were stopped and levofloxacin was started and continued for 3 weeks with resolution of symptoms. The culture was sent to the New York State Department of Health in Albany, NY, and identified as L. micdadei. Negative tests included normal transthoracic echo, normal head CT, and normal neck ultrasound. Five blood cultures, respiratory viral panel, urine Legionella antigen, Pneumocystis DNA PCR, Legionella culture from BAL, bacterial culture, fungal culture, Aspergillus antigen, and Histoplasma antigen were negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 31-year-old Caucasian female with autoimmune hepatitis and cirrhosis on prednisone and azathioprine presented with a 5-day history of fever, chills, shortness of breath, dry cough, and chest pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two months after starting oral prednisone (40 mg/day) and azathioprine (50 mg/day) for autoimmune hepatitis, and following two trips in the preceding 2 weeks to a hunting shack in northern New York, the patient presented with 5 days of fever, chills, dyspnea, dry cough, and chest pain. Her bilateral cavitary lung nodules progressed on serial chest CTs despite empirical vancomycin, meropenem, and amphotericin B.
subjective.past_medical_history: Ulcerative colitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, autoimmune hepatitis, and decompensated cirrhosis; treated with prednisone 40 mg daily and azathioprine 50 mg daily for 2 months. Born and raised in New York; visited a hunting shack in northern New York twice in the 2 weeks prior to illness; multiple negative PPD skin tests during nursing school.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, dyspnea, dry cough, and chest pain.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vitals: temperature 102 F, pulse 120 bpm, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, blood pressure 96/58 mmHg, and SpO2 >90% on 2 L/min supplemental oxygen. Initial physical examination was benign with clear lung auscultation.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 16,000/uL, neutrophils 14,400/uL), anemia (hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL), platelets 167,000/uL, ALT 62 U/L, AST 87 U/L, ALP 158 U/L, total bilirubin 13.2 mg/dL, and INR 2.9. Initial chest X-ray showed a trace left pleural effusion without infiltrates. Five blood cultures, urine culture, respiratory viral panel, urinary Legionella antigen, transthoracic echocardiogram, head CT, and neck ultrasound were all negative/normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT on hospital day 2 revealed small bilateral cavitary pulmonary nodules, which enlarged and increased in number with surrounding ground-glass opacities on repeat CT scans on days 3 and 9 despite meropenem, vancomycin, and amphotericin B. Bronchoscopy with BAL (day 4) was negative on Gram stain, fungal stain, bacterial/fungal/Legionella cultures, Pneumocystis PCR, and Aspergillus and Histoplasma antigen assays. However, CT-guided transthoracic core biopsy of a necrotic pulmonary nodule (performed on day 3) grew Legionella species on day 11, identified by the New York State Department of Health reference laboratory as Legionella micdadei.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Bilateral cavitary necrotizing pneumonia caused by Legionella micdadei mimicking invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in an immunosuppressed patient with autoimmune hepatitis and cirrhosis; invasive aspergillosis, histoplasmosis, and pneumocystosis were ruled out by negative Aspergillus/Histoplasma antigens, BAL fungal cultures, and lack of response to amphotericin B, and L. micdadei was definitively confirmed by CT-guided lung biopsy culture. Upon culture identification on hospital day 11, vancomycin, meropenem, and amphotericin B were discontinued and a 3-week course of levofloxacin was completed, achieving full clinical resolution.
